key_insight: Sample-based Krylov Quantum Diagonalization (SKQD) can estimate ground states of frustrated Heisenberg spin systems without variational optimization, achieving very high accuracy on small lattices and scaling to much larger ones than prior quantum studies.
engineering_relevance: The work shows a hardware-compatible path for near-term quantum simulation of strongly correlated spin models, with algorithmic tweaks that improve robustness under spin degeneracy and limited shot budgets.
method: Applied SKQD to the antiferromagnetic XXZ Heisenberg model on J1–J2 square, Kagome, and 1D chain lattices.
Used a ZZ deformation (Δ=2) to make the Hamiltonian sufficiently sparse for SKQD.
Added canonical bitstring compression and multiple Krylov subspaces to better recover configurations and improve ground-state coverage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sub-percent ground-state energy errors up to 24 spins, including 0.002% on the 12-site Kagome lattice, and extension to 72 spins with errors rising to about 19%–36% at the largest sizes.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades at larger system sizes, so results appear limited by shot budgets and circuit depth rather than the algorithm alone.
paper_title: Ground-state estimation of the Heisenberg model on frustrated lattices with Sample-based Krylov Quantum Diagonalization
